MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 11, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:01 p.m., on June 11, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 6, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Mayor Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch (via teleconference at 6:00 pm)
  Council Member Vasquez

Absent:  Council Member Bucknum

Staff Present:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P Curley III, City Attorney
  Elaine Lister, Director of Community Development
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE THE MEETING

At the hour of 5:03 pm Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting. Mayor Kelley reconvened the meeting
at 6:02 pm with three Council Members present, and Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch via teleconferencing.

INVOCATION: Council Member Vasquez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

City Council Minutes  1  June 11, 2024
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Santa Margarita Water District Update on Water Related Matters

  Received presentation from Santa Margarita Water District Board Member Frank Ury.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Paula Steinhauer, M.V.: Spoke out against the Pride Event that was held in the city and outlined
her opinions on the LGBTQ+ lifestyle.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Commended Council Member Vasquez and Commissioner Vichionne on
the pride event in Mission Viejo this past Saturday.

Debbie Bailey, M.V.; Danell Duran, M.V.; and Linda Roth, Lake Forest: Spoke out against
pickleball rate increase.

Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: Spoke on the Pride Event this past Saturday and stated she volunteered at
the event and spoke about the event.

Paola Trumbly, M.V.: Thanked all the vendors and volunteers at the Pride Event.

Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Spoke on the Pride Event and thanked Council Member Vasquez,
Commissioner Josh Vecchione, Dennis Wilberg, Paola Trumbly and the Diversity Inclusion
Task Force.

Lori Barragato, M.V.: Spoke on the Pride Event this past weekend and stated it was a wonderful
event.
.
Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Voiced the lack of transparency in the release of reports and Spoke on the
Memorandum of Understanding with the Netherlands and asked why there is no budget in place
or the itinerary for this tax funded excursion.

Jerry Toice, M.V.: Voiced his concerns regarding Age Wellness dropping their sponsorship of
Bingo at the Norman P. Community Center and asked that the Council help to bring bingo back
to the center.

Jerry Volomino, M.V.: Outlined the difference between Pride having a whole Month and why
Memorial Day has only one day. Spoke on the decline of our country’s value system and the
agenda to break us up and divide us.

Josh Vecchione, M.V.: Clarified the misinformation from previous speakers regarding the gay
and transgender community. He stated that the Pride Event was a family friendly event with
over 1300 residents in attendance.

City Council Minutes  2  June 11, 2024
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Item #16 was considered under separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to approve the remainder
of the Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Bucknum

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 28, 2024, as presented

2.  General Check Register Dated May 17, 2024, in the Amount of $1,575,338.86

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated May 24, 2024, in the Amount of $1,155,400.18

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated May 17, 2024, in the Amount of $11,290.30

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated May 24, 2024, in the Amount of $32,750.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2024

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for March 2024

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  June 11, 2024
 9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2024

  Received and filed.

10. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for March 2024

  Received and filed.

11. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report

  Received and filed.

  2024

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

14. Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Adopted Resolution 24-22 Providing for the Revisions to Select Personnel Policies.

15. Renewed Measure M (M2) Eligibility: Pavement Management Program Component

  Adopted Resolution 24-23 Concerning the Status and Update of the City of Mission Viejo's
  Pavement Management Plan for the Measure M (M2) Program, to Satisfy a Component of
  the City's Eligibility Requirements of the Orange County M2 Program.

17. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2024 - Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 24-24 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council
  to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing Protests;
  (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds in
  accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City Clerk
  to set the Public Hearing for August 27, 2024.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

City Council Minutes  4  June 11, 2024
 16. Irvine Boulevard/Trabuco Road Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Project
  (Project P) Cooperative Agreement

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon gave an update on the project.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
  Cooperative Agreement with the City of Irvine (A24-20) for the Irvine Boulevard / Trabuco
  Road Regional Traffic Signal Synchronization Project (CIP 24261).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

PUBLIC HEARINGS

18. Development Code Amendment P-DCA2024-0001 - A City-initiated petition for
  consideration of an amendment to Title 9 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code, to
  establish inclusionary housing requirements, as referenced in the Housing Plan of the
  Mission Viejo 6th Cycle (2021-2029) Housing Element. The project specifically
  includes: (1) an ordinance establishing inclusionary housing requirements for
  residential development projects; and (2) a resolution addressing a related in-lieu fee
  schedule as analyzed in a 2024 fee analysis.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Associate Planner Afshin Atapour
  presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 7:11 pm

  Michael Schlessinger, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the ordinance and that people having an
  affordable place to live and encouraged the Council to vote yes on this ordinance.

  Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Expressed his concerns that great teachers and other fine professionals
  are priced out of living here. He stated we need to attract and keep these young people in
  Mission Viejo and encouraged the Council to vote yes on this ordinance.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Thanked Elaine Lister and staff for their diligent work on this
  inclusionary housing requirement. -She shared concerns that our children and grandchildren
  will not have access to housing in our community. She expressed that we need teachers,
  hospital workers and young families in our community. Lastly, she thanked Council Member
  Vasquez and the others for sponsoring the Pride Event this past weekend.

  Barbara Casserly, M.V.: Thanked the members of the Mission Viejo Planning Partnership
  and expressed appreciation to the Kennedy Commission who advised this group. She also
  thanked Elaine Lister who did an excellent job on the housing element, and she looks forward
  to the Council approving this ordinance this evening.
City Council Minutes  5  June 11, 2024
   Adam Wook, BIA/OC: Stated that inclusionary zoning is a policy that kills more housing
  than it creates. He outlined his reasoning on this.

  Benjamin Hakim. M.V.: Voiced against affordable housing and how it only ends up with
  more expensive housing that still doesn’t provide for students and teachers. Gave reasons
  why he moved from Los Angeles to Mission Viejo and stated let’s be consistent with that
  and not try to be like Los Angeles.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 7:29 pm

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to (1) exempt the
  project from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to state CEQA
  guidelines Section 15061(b)(3); (2) introduce Ordinance 24-353 Approving P-DCA2024-
  000; and (3) adopt Resolution 24-25 Establishing Related Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fees.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

19. Appeal APL2024-001 filed by Mayor Trish Kelley and City Council Member Cynthia
  Vasquez of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s Approval of Conditional
  Use Permit P-CUP2023-003, Submitted by Miles Lemaire of Continuum Analytics, to
  Establish a Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Service and Office branch at 27741
  Crown Valley Parkway, Suite 205, Kaleidoscope, in the CH (Commercial Highway)
  Zone. The new DMV branch Proposes to Occupy 16,738 Square Feet in the
  Kaleidoscope Entertainment and Retail Complex. The conditional Use Permit was
  Approved by the Planning and Transportation Commission on May 13, 2024.

  Planning & Economic Development Manager Jennifer Lowe and Associate Planner Tim
  Martin gave the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the Public Hearing at 8:05 pm

  Miles Lemaire of Continuum Analytics spoke on behalf of the project and addressed
  concerns on the project.

  The following spoke out against the project: Anna Hornbostel, M.V.; Eric Nessa, M.V.;
  Benjamin Hakim, M.V.; Amy Balsz, M.V.; Patty McClendon, M.V.; Steve Eguina, M.V.;
  William Binckes, M.V.; Kylie and Blake Goold, M.V.; Marilyn MacDougall, M.V.; Lori
  Brooks, M.V.; Silvia Hoekstra, M.V.; Benjamin Hosseinian, M.V.; Jason Farris, M.V.; Eline
  Alson, M.V.; Jim Christian, M.V.

  Mayor Kelley closed the Public Hearing at 9:22 pm

City Council Minutes  6  June 11, 2024
   Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to adopt Resolution
  24-26 Approving Appeal Petition P-APL2024-001 And Denying Conditional Use Permit P-
  CUP2023-0003 Submitted by Miles Lemaire of Continuum Analytics to Establish a 16,738
  Square Foot Department of Motor Vehicles Service And Office Branch At 27741 Crown
  Valley Parkway, Suite 205, Kaleidoscope, In The Ch (Commercial Highway) Zone

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

RECESS

At the hour of 9:44 pm Mayor Kelley called a recess. The meeting reconvened at 9:52 pm.

OLD BUSINESS

20. Mission Viejo Library Display Schedule and Updates to Library Conduct Policy

  Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to (1)
  approve the Mission Viejo Library Display Schedule for the remainder of 2024, and (2)
  approve updates to Library Conduct Policy.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

21. Direction on Potential November 2024 Transient Occupancy Tax Ballot Measure

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Vasquez, to return to the City
  Council at the next meeting a Special Tax Ballot Measure on the November Ballot to provide
  funding for police, crime prevention, emergency response and maintenance of city
  infrastructure assets, including streets, sidewalks, storm drains, parks and trails, shall the
  measure increasing the transient occupancy tax paid only by hotel/motel/short-term rental
  guests from 8% to 12%.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  7  June 11, 2024
   AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

22. Animal Services Service Agreement with the City of Rancho Santa Margarita

  Animal Services Supervisor Kyle Werner presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, to approve
  the agreement for Animal Control and Shelter Services with the City of Rancho Santa
  Margarita (A24-21).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

23. Animal Services Service Agreement with the City of Laguna Hills

  Animal Services Supervisor Kyle Werner presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch, to approve
  the agreement for Animal Control and Shelter Services with the City of Laguna Hills (A24-
  22).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

NEW BUSINESS

24. Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Law Enforcement Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve the
  FY 2024-2025 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange (A24-23)
  for an amount not to exceed $24,436,299; and (2) approve funding in FY 2024-25 in the
  amount not to exceed $35,000 for overtime related to special enforcement services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
City Council Minutes  8  June 11, 2024
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Bucknum

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

25. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell complimented Mayor Kelley on her presentation at the Chamber of
Commerce State of the City held at the Arroyo Trabuco Golf Course. He also gave a presentation
on the efforts of the Olympic Committee. Council Member Goodell stated there was a community
meeting held at the Norman P Murray Center that was well attended by our local hotels, school
districts, Saddleback College and the Chamber of Commerce regarding the Sports and Economic
Tourism efforts. He also attended the Olympic Trial send-off event at the Marguerite Aquatics
Complex on Friday. He announced that the Swimming Olympic Trials will be held this weekend
in Indianapolis at the Lucas Oil Stadium and the Diving Olympic Trials will be held in Knoxville,
Tennessee this week as well. Council Member Goodell stated that he believes that we have 19
athletes participating in the trials for swimming and about 9 for diving. He wished all the best for
these athletes.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Grapes and Grains event and commented on how well
attended it was. She also attended the Olympic Trials Send-Off and then after that she went to the
Concert on the Green. Council Member Vasquez stated that she attended the Community of
Character event at Bathgate Elementary School. She announced that the first Mission Veijo Pride
Event was very well attended with over 1300 people which was really incredible, with 50 booths
that included 18 sponsors, food trucks and a great band. She stated that it was incredible how
much interest there is for 2025 and so far, they have raised about $17,000 which is an impressive
number considering they started at zero. Lastly, she concluded by saying how proud she is of how
things turned out.

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch touched upon his meeting with Waste Management to discuss how they
deal with recycling issues. He pointed out that that we used to send our recycle materials overseas,
but that is no longer the case and Waste Management showed their process and some other things
that are done which is very exciting and he assume at some point they will come to a future meeting
to discuss.

Mayor Kelley
City Council Minutes  9  June 11, 2024
 Mayor Kelley attended a hotel owner meeting at the Hampton Inn and Suites and will be meeting
with all three of our hotels to talk about how we can support them and how they can support us
with the various events coming to the city. She attended the Bushfire Kitchen opening and
encouraged residents to support our local restaurants. She also attended a Ribbon Cutting at Share
Ourselves and the Sports & Economic Tourism Committee Meeting. Mayor Kelley represented
the city at the League of California Cities Division Meeting, along with the Olympic Trials Send-
Off Event and the Concert on the Green. Lastly, she highlighted the Spirit League 20th Anniversary
Event at Newhart Middle School which is for developmentally disadvantaged athletes, and it was
great to see these athletes and families and all the work that goes into this event.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:33 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 25, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 25, 2024

City Council Minutes  10  June 11, 2024
